title: Mechanistic evolution across the C3–C4 continuum
positioning: Collaborative research project led by Dr. Chilperic Armel Foko Kuate on the coupled physiology and evolutionary accessibility of C3-like, C2/intermediate and C4-like phenotypes under environmental forcing.
browser_scope: Public browser pages expose research questions, provenance and reduced explanatory models. Unpublished equations, calibration material and full parameter sets remain outside the public release.
scientific_question: Starting from plausible C3-like populations, which combinations and sequences of anatomical, photorespiratory, biochemical, hydraulic and resource-allocation changes are physiologically viable and evolutionarily accessible under different environments?
process_layers: optional mechanistic C2 glycine/GDC photorespiratory pump
PEPC/C4-cycle recruitment and bundle-sheath CO2 concentration
replicated finite-population evolution with inheritance, mutation/segregation, selection and drift

analysis_boundary.optimization: CMA-ES, NSGA-II, grids and continuation map high-performance regions; optimizer iterations are not biological generations.
analysis_boundary.evolution: Only simulations with explicit inheritance, heritable variation, selection and drift are described as evolutionary trajectories.
analysis_boundary.c2: C2 is a mechanistic subregion of the continuum, not a mandatory label. It is included when glycine/GDC localization and associated carbon/nitrogen consequences are represented.
analysis_boundary.fitness: Assimilation is a physiological performance component, not reproductive fitness by itself.

public_outputs: historical optimization traces retained with corrected labels
local and global sensitivity analyses with model-revision provenance
limitations: No public figure establishes a natural evolutionary history by itself.
Species-level calibration and external validation are incomplete.
Genetic/mutational covariance and physiology-to-reproductive-fitness mapping remain major uncertainties.
Water-viscosity corrections do not replace pit, junction, outside-xylem, aquaporin or vulnerability effects.
Missing or nonphysical simulations must not be silently imputed as valid low-performance phenotypes.
